units.la: Figitur, heu, tristi ligno meus ardor Iesus: Et mea vita truci morte peremta cadit. Quàm fuit hic verus, nec ficti pectoris ardor: Cùm pro me lethi sponte subiuit onus! O vtinam dignas possem persoluere grates, Et possem hoc solo semper amore frui! O amor, ô noster, spes ô dulcissima, Iesu: Nos vt amas; sic te fac vt amare queam. Ah pereat, cui non amor hic magis omnibus vnus Sic placet, vt nullum quærat amorem alium. Te mihi Christe peto; nostri tu semper amorem Conserua: vt viuus te, moriens & amem.
units.tr: Alas, my ardour, Jesus, is nailed to the sad wood, and my life, destroyed by a cruel death, falls. How true was this ardour, not of a feigned heart, when of his own accord he took upon himself the burden of death for me! O that I could pay worthy thanks, and could always enjoy this one love! O love, our love, O sweetest hope, Jesus: as you love us, so make me able to love you. Ah, let him perish, for whom this love alone does not please more than all, so that he seeks no other love. You I ask for, Christ; keep your love for us always, so that living and dying I may love you.

units.la: I. C.
units.tr: I. C.

units.la: Fixus in hoc ligno meus est Amor vnus Iesus, Morte sua vitam qui mihi restituit. Ah vtinam dignas possem persoluere grates! Verùm opis hoc nostræ non satis esse scio. Spes mea Christe Deus, me respice: vt huius amoris, Quo foueor viuus, sim memor immoriens. Sic moriens viuam, sic vitam morte lucrabor; Nam tuus in vitam me revocabit amor.
units.tr: Fixed to this wood is my one love, Jesus, who by his death restored my life to me. Ah, that I could pay worthy thanks! But I know this is not enough for our need. My hope, Christ God, look upon me, that I may be mindful, even in dying, of this love by which I am cherished while living. So dying I shall live, and by death I shall gain life; for your love will call me back to life.

units.la: QVa putris intortis fundit se in brachia nodis Arbor, in infames noxa parata reos: Hîc regna: hîc arces: hîc nostri portus Amoris: Hîc vitæ fulcrum deliciumq; meæ. Hîc lethi spolium, partiq; insigne trophæi Christe tui: hîc sonti est ara parata gregi. Quæ pietas! hostes in partiiura triumphi, In partes regni Christe vocare tui! O flamma, ô amor, ô æterni fomes Amoris! Vitam è vulneribus vulneris autor habet. Fronde carens arbor pleno se germine prodit, Et radice carens vertice summa ferit. Quamq; notat præceps infami nomine vulgus, Hinc vitæ & famæ manat origo meæ. Nulla alia hos fructus, nulla hos tulit arbor Amores, Nec Libani tales procreat hortus opes. Et mortem dubitet quis pro crucis arce pacisci, In media noster si cruce regnat Amor?
units.tr: The rotten tree that spreads itself into twisted arms of knots, a harm made ready for infamous guilty men: here are kingdoms, here citadels, here the harbour of our love; here the support and delight of my life. Here is the spoil of death and the emblem of your trophy, Christ; here an altar is made ready for the guilty flock. What piety, to call enemies to share in your triumph, Christ, and into the parts of your kingdom! O flame, O love, O fuel of eternal love! The author of the wound has life from the wounds. The tree that lacks leaves shows itself in full growth, and though lacking root it strikes with its topmost crown. And what the headlong crowd marks with an infamous name, hence springs the origin of my life and reputation. No other tree bore these fruits, no other bore these loves, nor does the garden of Lebanon produce such riches. And who would hesitate to bargain for death in exchange for the citadel of the cross, if our love reigns in the midst of the cross?

units.la: CHriste tuo partos ne despice sanguine vernas, Qui vitæ hac ponunt in trabe fulcra suæ. Excute vitalem gelidis præcordibus ignem, Queis posita in Flamma est spes, salusq; tua. Nam quid? ad hunc si Christe tuum torpebimus ignem, Quis miseris poterit iam satis esse calor? CRVX TVA NOSTER AMOR: quid non speremus Aman- Fortius in media si cruce feruet amor. (res?
units.tr: Christ, do not despise the slaves born of your blood, who in this beam place the support of their life. Shake the vital fire out of cold hearts, in whom hope and your salvation are placed in the flame. For what? If we grow numb at this your fire, Christ, what warmth could ever be enough for wretched men? YOUR CROSS IS OUR LOVE: what may we not hope for, lovers, if love glows more strongly in the midst of the cross?
